criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001a: Identifies 24-month lookback deviation in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies the draft's 24-month service-standard lookback as conflicting with the APA's required 12-month lookback and proposes replacing it with the 12 months immediately preceding Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001b: Identifies 'or better than' qualifier in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft’s “at least equal to or better than” service standard as an upward-ratchet obligation, deletes it, and replaces it with the APA/playbook’s 12-month “substantially consistent” standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001c: Identifies undefined 'industry best practices' benchmark
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags “industry best practices” as an undefined external benchmark that conflicts with the APA/playbook and creates an expansive performance guarantee. It proposes deleting that language and replacing it with the APA’s 12-month “substantially consistent” historical service standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001d: Proposes redline conforming service standard to playbook
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent proposes express replacement language in Section 3.1 requiring services to be provided “in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with” how they were provided to the Business during the twelve months immediately preceding Closing, which conforms to the playbook standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002a: Identifies liability cap as 200% of total fees vs. APA's trailing 12-month cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies the draft cap as 200% of total Service Charges/fees paid and contrasts it with APA Section 7.12(d)'s rolling trailing-12-month cap based on fees actually paid during the 12 months preceding the claim. It also proposes conforming replacement language and quantifies the exposure difference.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002b: Quantifies liability cap exposure difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly quantifies the liability-cap exposure: approximately $41.004 million under the draft versus $13.464 million under the APA trailing-12-month cap, a difference of $27.540 million (about 3.05x). It also provides an apples-to-apples corrected-fee comparison.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002c: Redlines liability cap to conform to APA Section 7.12(d)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent proposes corrective redline language in Section 10.1 capping each party’s aggregate liability at the TSA fees actually paid during the 12 months immediately preceding the date the applicable claim is first asserted, expressly aligning the cap with APA Section 7.12(d).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003a: Identifies non-mutual consequential damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies Section 10.2 as a unilateral/one-way consequential damages waiver that protects Trident but leaves Polaris exposed, and proposes replacing it with a mutual waiver.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003b: Redlines to make consequential damages waiver mutual
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 expressly replaces the unilateral waiver with mutual language stating that “each Party” waives claims against the other for consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, and punitive damages, consistent with the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004a: Identifies automatic renewal extending TSA beyond 18 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies the two automatic six-month renewals as potentially extending the TSA from the 18-month initial term to 30 months, states that this conflicts with APA §7.12(a)'s 18-month cap, and proposes deleting automatic renewal.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004b: Redlines to delete auto-renewal and impose hard 18-month stop
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly deletes automatic renewal and provides that the TSA expires after the 18-month Initial Term. It permits only a mutually agreed written extension for an individual service, limited to six additional months and priced at cost-plus 15%, satisfying the stated criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005a: Identifies 120-day termination notice exceeding APA's 90 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags Section 5.3's 120-day prior written notice for terminating individual services as conflicting with APA Section 7.12(c)'s 90-day notice period and proposes replacing it with 90 days.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005b: Redlines termination notice to 90 days per APA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly redlines Section 5.3 by replacing the 120-day termination notice with a 90-day prior written notice and cites APA Section 7.12(c) as the basis.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006a: Identifies Key Personnel consent right overriding Polaris staffing discretion
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags Sections 4.3 and Schedule H as improperly giving Trident prior-consent rights over reassignment, removal, and replacement of Key Personnel, explains that this conflicts with Polaris's sole staffing discretion under the playbook, and proposes deleting those consent and approval rights.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006b: Proposes compromise on Key Personnel (notice + qualified replacement)
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline restores Polaris’s sole discretion over staffing and removes Trident’s consent right, while offering a reasonable compromise: advance notice where practicable and identification or assignment of a reasonably qualified replacement. Sections 4.3 and Schedule H expressly implement this approach.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007a: Identifies IT services 15% markup exceeding APA 10% cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the IT Services 15% markup and $391,000 monthly fee as exceeding APA §7.12(b)'s 10% cap, and corrects the fee to $374,000 per month.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007b: Correctly computes IT fee difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly calculates the IT fee overcharge as $17,000 per month ($391,000 minus $374,000) and $306,000 over 18 months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007c: Notes APA compliance risk even though overcharge benefits Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly notes that the 15% IT markup economically benefits Polaris but violates APA §7.12(b)'s 10% cap and must be corrected. It also explains that correction preserves Polaris's credibility and avoids a potential challenge to the fee schedule.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008a: Identifies audit frequency deviation (twice/year vs. once/12 months)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft permits audits twice per calendar year and proposes revising the provision to allow audits no more than once in any 12-month period, consistent with the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008b: Identifies audit cost allocation deviation (Seller's vs. Buyer's expense)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft makes audits seller-funded/at Service Provider's expense, cites the playbook deviation, and proposes revised language making audits at Trident's sole expense, subject to reimbursement only if an overcharge exceeds 5%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008c: Identifies audit notice period deviation (10 vs. 30 business days)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags the draft’s 10 Business Days’ audit notice as too short and proposes redlining Section 14.1–14.2 to require at least 30 Business Days’ prior written notice, citing the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009a: Identifies Ohio governing law vs. playbook's Pennsylvania law
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags the draft's Ohio governing law and cites the playbook, then proposes replacing it with Pennsylvania law in Sections 15.1–15.2. The review memo likewise identifies Ohio law as the deviation and Pennsylvania law as the seller's proposed fix.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009b: Identifies Cuyahoga County litigation vs. playbook's AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags the draft’s Ohio/Cuyahoga County court litigation provision as a deviation and proposes Pennsylvania law with confidential binding arbitration under the AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009c: Explains strategic importance of home-state law and arbitration for Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly explains the strategic rationale: Ohio litigation creates a buyer-home-state and public-docket disadvantage, while Pennsylvania law and confidential AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh reduce home-court, discovery, and confidentiality risks for Pittsburgh-based Polaris.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010a: Identifies overbroad perpetual IP license grant
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags Section 7.1’s perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license, including modification, derivative-work, and sublicensing rights, as a significant and fundamental departure from the no-license position. It identifies proprietary tools, methodologies, software, and know-how as exposed to material IP leakage and proposes deleting the grant and limiting access to the TSA term solely to receive services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010b: Redlines to delete IP license and confirm Polaris sole ownership
criteria_results.reasoning: The output deletes the perpetual, irrevocable license and replaces it with language stating that all Service Provider Materials remain Polaris’s sole and exclusive property. It grants no license or ownership interest beyond Trident’s limited, term-bound access and use solely to receive the Services, with access ending upon termination or expiration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011a: Identifies missing non-solicitation provision
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft omits a non-solicitation provision and proposes a new Section 15.12 prohibiting Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris personnel who provided services under the TSA.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011b: Drafts non-solicitation provision with 12-month post-service tail
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed Section 15.12 prohibits Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris service personnel during the Term and for 12 months after termination or expiration, unless Polaris gives prior written consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012a: Identifies CGL insurance reduction ($2M vs. $5M playbook)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft requires only $2 million in CGL coverage and proposes increasing Buyer’s CGL coverage to $5 million per occurrence and aggregate, consistent with the playbook requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012b: Identifies missing umbrella coverage requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft has no umbrella coverage and proposes adding $5 million in umbrella/excess coverage in Section 13.1 and the review memorandum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012c: Identifies missing additional insured endorsement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft lacks additional-insured protection and proposes requiring Polaris to be named as an additional insured under Buyer's CGL and umbrella policies, with certificates and endorsements delivered after closing and annually.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013a: Flags missing IMMEX program provisions for Monterrey facility
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft lacks an allocation for maintaining the Monterrey facility's IMMEX certification and proposes detailed language assigning primary responsibility and costs to Trident, with defined transition assistance and notice obligations for Polaris.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013b: Flags missing Mexican data privacy (LFPDPPP) provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the TSA is limited to U.S. privacy law and omits Mexican LFPDPPP requirements for Monterrey employee HR/payroll data. It proposes a controller/processor allocation, compliant privacy notices (avisos de privacidad), required consents or lawful cross-border transfer mechanisms, security and breach obligations, and a data-processing addendum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014a: Identifies missing termination assistance/wind-down provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft is silent on termination assistance/wind-down and proposes a new Section 5.5 providing reasonable, bounded transition assistance for up to 60 days, consistent with the Polaris playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014b: Proposes termination assistance at cost-plus-15% for up to 60 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed New Section 5.5 expressly provides termination assistance for no more than 60 days at cost-plus-15% pricing and includes drafted wind-down support language.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015a: Identifies missing change order procedure
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft lacks a formal change-order process and explains the risk of informal scope expansion. It proposes a written, dual-signature change order procedure for out-of-scope services, material volume increases, new deliverables, and other material changes, consistent with the playbook.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015b: Proposes change order procedure with cost-plus-15% pricing
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed new Section 6.7 requires a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both parties for out-of-scope services, material volume increases, new deliverables, or material changes, and states that additional services are priced at cost-plus 15% unless otherwise agreed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016a: Identifies vague payment terms ('commercially reasonable time')
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags “commercially reasonable time” as vague and unacceptable, explains the resulting cash-flow and enforcement risk, and replaces it with a defined Net 30 payment deadline (with Net 45 as a fallback).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016b: Redlines payment terms to Net 30 days
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.3 replaces the vague payment timing with payment of each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after the invoice date, which satisfies the Net 30 requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016c: Adds late payment interest at 1.5%/month or max legal rate
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.3 expressly adds that late amounts accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017a: Identifies missing force majeure 90-day termination trigger
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft force majeure clause lacks a termination trigger and proposes allowing either party to terminate the affected service without penalty after 90 consecutive days of a materially affecting force majeure event.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017b: Proposes 90-day force majeure termination right
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed Article 12 language states that if a force majeure event continues for 90 consecutive days and materially affects a service, either party may terminate the affected service without penalty on written notice.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo produced as a deliverable
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes a clearly labeled seller-side TSA review memorandum that summarizes the key TSA issues, risks, proposed fixes, and negotiation strategy.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo organizes issues by priority tiers (Critical/Significant/Minor)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo clearly organizes issues into three priority tiers: Section 2 is labeled “Critical,” Section 4 is labeled “Significant,” and Section 5 is labeled “Minor.”

criteria_results.title: APA-conflict issues classified as highest priority in cover memo
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly places the identified direct APA conflicts in Section 2, titled “Critical — direct APA conflicts or closing-level issues,” and marks the 200% liability cap, automatic renewals beyond the 18-month limit, 120-day termination notice, and 15% IT markup as “Must-change.” It separately categorizes playbook deviations as merely “Significant,” so the APA conflicts are clearly assigned the highest priority.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo includes negotiation strategy distinguishing firm vs. flexible positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo clearly distinguishes firm from flexible positions for well over three key issues and explains the basis. It labels direct APA conflicts as “Must-change,” treats the perpetual IP license and staffing discretion as firm/non-starters, and identifies negotiable fallbacks for termination assistance, change-order pricing, payment terms, insurance, audits, force majeure, dispute resolution, and non-solicitation. The recommended negotiation sequence and trading-points section further separates non-negotiable APA/IP/Mexico protections from implementation details where compromise is acceptable.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes proposed edits to the TSA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes extensive section-by-section proposed redline edits to the TSA, with explicit deletions, additions, and substitutions to draft language, rather than merely listing issues.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes explanatory comments for changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline includes extensive explanatory comments for each substantive proposed edit, identifying the basis (such as specific APA sections, playbook provisions, and client instructions), the risk if unchanged, and negotiability. These bracketed/anchored comments and corresponding comment boxes satisfy the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Polaris as Service Provider / Seller throughout
criteria_results.reasoning: The output consistently identifies Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. as the Seller and Service Provider, identifies Trident as the Buyer/Service Recipient, and frames all proposed revisions to protect Polaris’s provider-side interests. No material party-role confusion appears.

criteria_results.title: References APA Section 7.12 when flagging APA-conflict issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The output repeatedly cites APA Section 7.12 and its relevant subsections when flagging APA conflicts, including §7.12(a) for term/renewal, §7.12(c) for termination notice, §7.12(b) for the fee markup cap, and §7.12(d) for the liability cap and damages waiver.

criteria_results.title: Fee escalation provision addressed (playbook: greater of 3% or CPI-U)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly addresses fee escalation in Section 6.4 / Schedule G §5, cites Playbook §4.2, and proposes annual fee increases by the greater of 3% or the CPI-U increase for the preceding 12 months. The review memo also repeats this opening position.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification provision addressed (Buyer indemnifies for third-party claims)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly addresses indemnification in Sections 9.1–9.3 and proposes that Buyer/Service Recipient indemnify Seller for third-party claims arising from Buyer's use of or reliance on the services, Buyer's breach, or Buyer's wrongful acts, except to the extent caused by Seller's gross negligence or willful misconduct. This aligns with the stated playbook position.

criteria_results.title: Both deliverable files are produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes two clearly distinct deliverables: a seller-side redlined TSA labeled “tsa-markup-redline.docx” and a separate partner cover/review memorandum labeled “tsa-review-memo.docx.”

criteria_results.title: Correct total monthly service cost baseline ($1,020,000) referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies the total monthly base cost as $1,020,000 and the corrected aggregate monthly fee at a 10% markup as $1,122,000, including a fee table showing the component amounts and correct sum.

criteria_results.title: Playbook's dispute escalation to senior executives referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly proposes that disputes first be escalated to the parties’ CFO or General Counsel representatives for 15 Business Days before confidential AAA arbitration. The review memo also references executive escalation in the recommended dispute-resolution process.

criteria_results.title: Redline comments explain specific risk to Polaris for at least five changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline comments identify concrete adverse consequences to Polaris for well over five distinct issues. Examples include up to $27.54 million in additional liability exposure under the proposed cap, permanent leakage and sublicensing of Polaris IP, workforce and operational constraints from staffing approval rights, indefinite service obligations from automatic renewal and force majeure provisions, cash-flow risk from vague payment terms, Mexican privacy and IMMEX compliance exposure, and disruptive audits into proprietary systems. These comments go beyond merely citing the APA or playbook.
